current_example.problem:
The figure below shows the graph of $f(x).$ Evaluate $\lim_\limits{x \to \,4} f(x).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227428/assets/168433761f6629ad555a70acf5764f93246484c253f3c7ecba8fdfdfd87c2adf.png)
current_example.worked_solution:
We see from the graph that as $x$ approaches $4$ from the left, the function $f(x)$ approaches $-\infty.$ So, the left-hand limit is

$$
\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 4^-} f(x) = -\infty \, .
$$

Likewise, as $x$ approaches $4$ from the right, the function $f(x)$ again approaches $-\infty.$ So, the right-hand limit is

$$
\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 4^+} f(x) = -\infty \, .
$$

Consequently,

$$
\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 4} f(x)=-\infty \, .
$$
